title: #76: Post findings outside the changed lines as file-level comments
body:
Closes #76.

A finding too far from any added line (more than the 2-line snap from #75), in a file in the reviewed diff, now posts as a **file-level** review comment instead of an `unanchorable` summary blocker. The comment's badge names the line (`` `high` · documentation · line 64, outside the changed lines ``). The title stays the first line, so the thread matches re-reports and waivers by title: a file-level thread has no line.

- **Same rules as inline comments:** thresholds, merge, cap and `Waive:`/resolve all apply. Cross-push dedup counts a file-level comment while its file is still in the diff. The fix is always prose.
- **Files outside the diff:** a finding there still can't take a comment, and stays a location-only summary blocker.
- **Verifier:** it is told a file-level thread covers the whole file and that the comment names the line. Before, a null line read as "outdated".
- **GitHub adapter:** create-review's `comments[]` can't be file-level, so when there are file comments the adapter creates a pending review, adds each file thread with `addPullRequestReviewThread(subjectType: FILE)`, then submits. `listReviews` hides pending reviews, so a half-built review never satisfies the marker check. Every publish first deletes a pending review an earlier attempt left behind, because GitHub allows only one per user.
- **Summary wording:** "commented inline" now reads "commented on".
- REQUIREMENTS §7.2, §9.1, §9.2, §9.3 and §9.4 are updated.

**Not covered by tests:** the real adapter path (pending review, file threads, submit), because the fake GitHub only records reviews. It needs a check on a live PR before relying on it.

expected.defect: A review with a file-level finding fails to publish, so the new comment never reaches the PR.
